This version also has everything from 2.1.1, including the app in Spanish.

**New: the app can stay in the system tray**
- Closing the Nilesoft Shell Pro window now leaves the app running in the system tray, the area next to the clock. Click its icon to open the window again. Right-click it for *Open Nilesoft Shell Pro*, *Check for updates*, *Restart Explorer* and *Quit*.
- The app starts with Windows, in the tray, without opening its window. It doesn't need administrator rights, and it only applies to your Windows account.
- While it is in the tray, the app checks for updates shortly after Windows starts and then about every eight hours. When a new version is out you get a Windows notification: *Nilesoft Shell Pro 2.x is available. Click to see what's new.* Clicking it opens the app on Home, where the update banner is. You are told once about each version, and never about a version you skipped. *Check for updates automatically*, the *Beta* channel and *Download and install updates automatically* work as before.
- Starting the app again from the Start menu opens the window you already have, also when it is in the tray.
- In the tray the app draws nothing and uses little memory. It wakes up only for its icon and the update checks.

**You decide**
- *Preferences > Startup and tray* has two switches, both on by default: *Keep Nilesoft Shell Pro in the system tray* and *Start with Windows*. Turn off the first one and the app works like before: closing the window ends it, there is no tray icon, and it doesn't start with Windows.
- The app sets up starting with Windows once, the first time you run this version. If you turn it off, in the app or in Windows (*Settings > Apps > Startup* or Task Manager), it stays off.
- Uninstalling the MSI closes the app and removes the start with Windows entry. For a portable copy, turn off *Keep Nilesoft Shell Pro in the system tray* before you delete its folder.
- Docs: [Startup and tray](https://abdullah-masood-05.github.io/Shell/app/preferences/#startup-and-tray).
